Helldivers: Smells like… Freedom
Oh man, oh man, oh man. Helldivers. There is so much I could say about this game I don’t even know where to start!
I guess I should start by saying, this game has a LOT going for it! Like being made by the duders that made Magicka! A wonderfully fun, and funny, game that I love. And the Showdown Effect, another great game I love. Arrowhead has a great track record of really good games.
Helldivers also has a great Sci-fi setting, which I am super fond of. Better yet, it pokes fun at the classics, like Starship Troopers ( and in some ways Warhammer, StarCraft, etc.) which the devs has cited as a large inspiration. According to Reddit, anyway. Also it has a wonderful sense of humor, just like the previous Arrowhead games. And, and get this: it’s really, really, well made incredibly fun and rewarding! Triple threat!
At the time of writing I started playing this game a week ago… Look at my playtime… Yeah.
Now, what is Helldivers? Well I’m glad you asked!… Or that I posed the question? Anyway, Helldivers is a top down twin-stick shooter that has you playing as the titular Helldivers. A group of ‘elite’ soldiers sent in from orbit behind enemy lines to shuck fit up.
You do this by dropping in from orbit via hellpods. Think Space paratroopers ala the ODST, Starship Troopers, Imperial Stormtroopers, Space Marines or whatever your favorite Sci-Fi equivalent is. And then you go and perform various objectives around the procedurally generated maps on planet.
Sounds easy right? Heh… well, about that. This game is hard. Like… it can give you a headache hard.
Especially if you’re playing with Randoms who have no regard for advanced military tactics such as basic teamwork. But there are some really good players out there! And the game is brand-spankin’ new, so the community is still pretty tight knit. So that’s good, but this game really shines with a buddy. Especially in a local co-op setting. Some of the funniest moments in Helldivers are when your mech falls from orbit and unexpectedly lands on your friend splattering them into a greasy puddle of barely masked anger and disappointment..
There is a brief moment of shock as the red mist settles… “crap, sorry.”
My friend and I played fifteen hours of Helldivers over the weekend. It was one of the best gaming experiences I’ve had in years.
Anyway accidental friend manslaughter aside, the game has twelve mission types which are variations on “Go here and: protect this thing, blow this thing up, move this thing, escort these things, reactivate these things, kill this thing etc.” They are rather similar, but they have enough variety to not become same-y. Which is great. The really nice thing is that the maps are all procedurally generated, so even if they have the same feel, they’re never the same. And each mission will have up to something like seven objectives to complete depending on the difficulty, so there’s never not something to do!
And there are also two different types of missions! There are the normal drops, and then ‘retaliatory strikes’. Where you are fighting waves of enemies in a smaller arena like map.
And they’re incredibly hard… Truthfully… They’re a major ♥♥♥♥♥.
Now, as well as having tons of content to do. Helldivers also has a persistent campaign!
Every time you perform a successful drop you add influence to the galactic war. Which is a three front war against the enemies of Super Earth, and Managed Democracy. Each front consists of a number of ‘systems’ with planets that need to be liberated. This is your job, and the payoff of successful drops being that you take the system and advance towards a specific enemy’s homeworld.
Currently, in war 12, we are on the doorstep of each of the three enemy factions. The Cyborg, a faction of… cyborgs. Think the Strogg from quake! As well as the Bugs, big♥♥♥♥♥unholy space lobsters bent on eating your squishy parts. They’re the bugs from Starship Troopers, and the Tyranid rolled into a nice neat package. And then there’s the Illumanite. Ancient Aliens who can teleport, have powerful shields, and mind altering abilities.
Each faction feels different, and have their sets of strengths and weaknesses. Personally I love fighting the Cyborgs. They’re really fun and their units have lots of heavy armor, meaning Anti-Tank is a high priority. The bugs are hard to kill and swarm you in seconds. Bug Spray recommended. And the Illuminate can be invisible, attack with snipers, and teleport.
Odds are you will die. A lot. Like… A lot…
And that’s one of the reasons this game is so wonderful. When you overcome the enemy and find a strategy that works it’s incredibly rewarding. Every successful mission is met with high-fives and fist pumps.
The wonderful feeling that running through a difficult mission gives is nigh addicting… Calling in mechs, tanks, rockets, artillery, frantically shooting enemies, reviving comrades, working together as a cohesive unit… It’s great.*
*Basic teamwork skills required.
There is a wonderful amount of stuff in Helldivers, plenty of weapons, lots of different ways to rain death upon your foes, and some sick cape physics, yo.
And, get this, it’s only $19.99.
Helldivers is totally worth the price. I would recommend it to anyone who likes challenging multiplayer games, and has a Sci-Fi bent. Plus Arrowhead is awesome and deserve the support. This amazing game was made by a team of 10 – 12! That’s super cool!
But, my gushing aside; This game is good. Like… If I had played it more in 2015 it would be my GOTY.
I’ve never played a game and thought “Yeah, I want to buy all of your DLC… I’m going to buy all of the DLC.”
And I did.

This is probably the most fun Rogue-like game you will ever play. I think the challenge is what makes this game so great. Disregard the hours that Steam shows ive played, that is just on my new PC. I bought the online humble bundle and probably played around 200 hours throughout my senior year high school classes. Even with so much time spent playing, this game will still bend me over, and it doesn't use lube.
Ok, now to the gameplay mechanics.
The Ships.
- The unlock style of the ships is amazing. Can't beat the boss with a ship to get the next one? Then just figure out the random events that will unlock the ship. Even with there being 10 ships (8 of them with 3 variations, 2 of them with 2 variation), each ship's play style is unique and requires different strategies to be successful.
The Weapons
- The different kinds of weapons also cater to the individuals play style. From Missles, to beams, to lasers, there are so many different combinations that work well together depending on the ship build. Even the best weapons aren't too overpowered, they are balanced well so that there is no "Guaranteed Win".
The NPCs
- Each race has specefic advantages, and disadvantage, which means a healthy mix is suggested. And through the extra long and tough games you may find yourself becoming attached to your crew members. There have been tears shed when a faithful crew has met an early demise.
The all powerful RNG
- The unpredictability of this game is probably the most important feature. Literally everything is dictated by the RNG. And believe me, you can be having your best game yet and out of nowhere the RNG will literally crap on your hopes and dreams.
Conlusion
- I hope I have convinced you to buy this game, because what else are you looking for in a single player game than:          ------Unlimited replay value
------A challenge level so high you will have an aneurysm at least once
------Seriously do you need more reasons than I have already given.
So buy this game, and if you need any advice, head on over to
Seriously buy it now.

Perfect for what it wants to be, which is a supernatural, eerie mystery, with almost the most breathtaking graphics in a game.
It's a bit short, and not very difficult, but the narrative and world design supplement the lack of challenge.
It warns you that it doesn't hold your hand, and it rather takes that to an extreme.  There is no guidance of any sort, really.  And the world is full of intricately detailed places you don't need to go.  On the one hand, that feels realistic, and on the other hand, it can be a bit annoying.
My only real complaint is the saving system.  You have to wait for an auto save, and that happens when you do something in the story, or after certain actions such as going on a lift or reading certain documents.  I don't see the point in not giving the player a manual save.  It's not as if you can die or even fail.
Overall, great experience, if a bit short (I'll be honest, the length for this sort of experience is actually perfect).  An absolute joy to walk through its levels, and a compelling mystery and story.

This falls into the genre of "First Person Looker" in my book.  Very basic puzzling, but the main game mechanic is walking around looking at the pretty scenery.
This feels like a very open ended sort of world, explore where you want and solve what you can.  Except...it isn't really.
At the end of the game, you are basically presented with a status meter and if you want to proceed you need to back track throughout the world and solve all those puzzles you didn't notice or solve the first time.  While the game isn't exactly huge, it is incredibly tedius to backtrack for 10-15 minutes just to wonder around looking for something to let you know there is even a puzzle here.
I had to resort to using a walkthrough/guide to finish because I lost patience after backtracking.
OK, well that is the mechanic review. But really the game is a story, so how does that stack up?  Not really very compelling.  The ending is intentionally ambiguous.  But it also makes me feel like nothing I just did really mattered.

I topped off this game in about two and a half hours, maybe three, and I was going at a semi leisurely pace. Occasionally I'd hop around a whole course if I saw an opening, but I fell off the map more times than I can count, so I guess that balances it out.
All in all, I loved it. The mechanics seemed tailored to my style of movement (Long hours of Titanfall, CoD: AW, Mirror's Edge and such) and the learning curve/time to get used to the controls was almost non-existent. The controls themselves are well placed, with left click being your grapple and right click being your 'booster' ability charger, either jump or sprint jump. Jump at spacebar and, later, jet pack when airborne. I had more fun playing around bouncing off walls with the grapple than I did actually doing some of the puzzles.
Bringing me to the puzzles, I found a few that were frustrating, namely the one where Maddie challenges you to go through a whole course without using your grapple. It's possible, fun even, but I must have tried thirty times before I figured it out and quit derping. I'm not one for puzzle platformers, though, so ignore that particular bit if you have experience.
Final conclusion: grab it if it's on sale, as thirteen bucks is a bit much. I got it on humble bundle and can honestly say it was worth paying over the average for, including all the other games I got with it. I'd say eight would be the most I'd pay for it, knowing what would be waiting for me. The story is a touch shallow and the voice acting isn't stellar, but for a simple indie game it's far from terrible.
TL;DR: Buy it on sale, blitz it in one go, come back on occasion if your internet craps out. Solid recommendation.

Rock 'N' Roll Defense is tower defense game. The concept is simple: build your towers and protect your kingdom. In this game the towers are speakers and the kingdom is a stage with a rock band playing a concert. You must protect them of pop, country, and etc fans. The idea is interesting but some points of the game annoy you too much.
To pass some levels you need luck, not ability, not the right towers, you need LUCK, it♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥me off. There are a few kind of enemies in each world (the game has 4 worlds), some of the enemies moves fast than others, so the obvious would be the fastest ones coming first than others, right? Not in this game.
I don't remember what level was, but there were 4 kind of enemies, let name them 1 2 3 and 4. 1 and 2 are the fastest ones, which mean you need a powerful tower (speaker) to kill them easily and don't let them get into stage, it was what I planned, built the speakers I thought necessary and started the level, to my surprise the ones who came first were the slowest ones, and when they were in the range of the speakers the fastest appeared, and guess what? They continued their way to the stage without getting any shot, it made me reset the level, because if any enemy successful get in the stage, you can no longe receive the max stars for the level.
I needed to reset 6-7 times until the fastest ones came first and I finally passed the level. And if the enemies came in a random order, it is pretty unfair, because in the beggining of each level you do not have money to build a lot of speakers, so you can kill 1 or 2 enemies togethers, not 4-5.
The game had 9 achievements (If i am correct) in the first time I bet it, recently it received an update and now it has 240 achievements. I installed again to check what was changed and I needed to pass every level again. To my unhapiness, the new achievements has nothing relationed with the game, they are simple a try to sell the game, because now the achievements are letters and symbols, but have no relation with the game. An example of that: I killed 100 enemies and the achievement I got was the meme "Lenny Face".
There are 8 speakers, I needed just 4 to beat the game in the first time I played it, and I just needed the same 4 to beat the game in the second time, the others are just useless, you just need to use if you want to test something new, but they are not necessary to pass any level.
Last but not least; the game crashed a lot of times, sometimes I was almost passing a level and whoah! the game crashed and I lost my progress in that specific level. Honestly, Rock 'N' Roll Defense could be a good game, but it need so many improves, the new achievements were a totally unnecessary update.
I do not recommend buying Rock "N' Defense, not now, perhaps one day it will become a playable game and people will be able to enjoy the game; but for now, you should look to another tower defense game, one which will not get you stressed.

SanctuaryRPG: Black Edition is a humorous and strategic turn-based dungeon crawling ASCII adventure. Drawing heavy inspiration from both Roguelikes and Japanese RPGs, the game offers a robust action-RPG inspired combat system.
You know those old B movies you saw at the drive-in, or those old sci-fi flicks that are now in the Public Domain? SanctuaryRPG is like that, and it is meant to be that. It doesn’t try and be some AAA game produced by some ridiculously large studio. No, SanctuaryRPG is a wonderful mess of self-deprecating satire, and that’s what makes it so perfect for a text-based RPG.
: The precise formula for a comedic, but intriguing, story that’ll keep you enticed.
: 9/10
No, I’m not going to tell you that the graphics are terrible because there’s no fancy SSAA or SSAO. SanctuaryRPG relishes in the wonderful world of ASCII art that is detailed and beautiful. Not only that but the game manages to include secrets within the backdrop of symbols that fit naturally. It works, and it works wonderfully!
: Simple and old-school graphics are a throwback to a forgotten era of games.
: 9/10
You can play the whole game with a keyboard, and at no time are controls hidden behind memory. It might take a little time to get used to because of the mechanics, but you are never timed in your decisions. They nailed down solid controls that work well and are always visible.
: Simple to use and never hidden.
: 9/10
A myriad of old and newer sounds come together to form the nostalgic, synth-ridden soundtrack of SanctuaryRPG. It’s fun, engaging, and varies enough to keep things fresh during your various adventures. On top of the soundtrack you have the familiar sound effects one would expect from a text-based RPG.
: It’s honestly a really nice soundtrack with some great sound effects to go along with it. It fits well!
: 8.5/10
As with any rogue-like game, SanctuaryRPG’s difficulty lies in both skill and learning from your mistakes. It does this quite fairly, and with the right planning one is able to go far without worry of some nonsensical one-hit kill or unfair mechanic. There are always humorous things that can happen against your favour, but I think that’s part of the charm. I found my time with SanctuaryRPG to be balanced and fair, but still always difficult.
: Just the right amount of reward for just the right amount of saltiness!
: 9/10
One could say that a single hour of gameplay is not enough to judge the scale of an RPG like this game, but do not be fooled; I have spent many more hours on this game without Steam. I can assure you that SanctuaryRPG is deep and offers such a large variety of gameplay and fun that it’s worth twice the price to me (at least).

Flame over is a heroic, yet very bright and colorful roguelike game.  It definitely has a unique premise, but is the gameplay compelling enough?  I've had a chance to play it for a few hours so let's  find out in this first impression.
In Flame Over you play as a firefighter named Blazer Carruthers and quite simply you put out the fires.  It's a roguelike, which means levels are procedural generated and death is permanent.  In Flame Over there are four different game zones that are very similar in design, but have different looks.  You start off in the fire station and make your way through the levels, putting out as much of the fire as you can. Using the right trigger you shoot water from your hose and the left trigger uses the extinguisher.  You need to use the water kfor big fires and the extinguisher to eliminate electrical fires.  It's interesting how you need more than one tool to get the job done.  Your supplies run out, but there are refills at the base and throughout the level.  What's also interesting is that you can find an emergency shut off for electricity which will end electrical fires.
Along your way you'll run into people who need help escaping.  When you bring them back you gain additional time to complete your objective.  There's also the stereotypical firefighter saving a cat motif when you randomly find cats to save.  Some people will ask you to find their personal belongings, but you are too damn busy saving everyone in the building! Put out all the fires, head to exit, and you'll get your reward.  When you put out fires you'll receive money that you can use for special items and different types of buffs.
The art style of Flame Over is very suitable.  It softens the theme of saving people from a burning building and keeps the game fun instead of dramatic.  The flame effect looks nice and is very easy to spot when you enter the room.  For an isometric roguelike, this game looks very attractive.  Textures look detailed and the flame effects are perfect for the setting.
You may think this game is a cakewalk, but it's not.  There is definitely high challenge as fires spread and reform rapidly if you don't extinguish the entire room.  You'll be surprised how fast the game moves once you are in the inferno.  There's plenty of resource management between saving civilians and rationing your supplies.  You'll never find yourself with downtime during rounds.  The action is perfectly balanced.
Flame Over is a surprisingly fun and charming game.  You get to be a real hero for once and save lives, but the game doesn't take itself to seriously.  It's only $12 on Steam and although the amount of zones are small, the game does have re-playability since it's a roguelike.  If this game looks like it fits your style, you may want to check it out.  I recommend it.

If you're looking for a charming, fun challenge, I highly recommend Flame Over.

"Flame Over features a dynamic fire system that burns and spreads according to the materials found in each randomly generated level. Watch fires spread according to the materials available, attacking your fire fighter and generating dangerous hazards across 4 game zones."
The game was developed by Laughing Jackal and Published by Ghostlight. The game will release on the 28th May 2015. The cost of the game is $11.99/£8.99. The game will also release in the future for PS4 and is already out on the PS Vita. There are a total of 36 Steam achievements.
In the game you control a fire-fighter, or better known by his name "Blaze". With Blaze you must go around buildings which are randomly generated each time putting out the fires, saving humans and of course cats. Certain fires require certain types of extinguisher, Water gets rid of general fire and stops it spreading however for electrical fires you can only stop with foam. It is well worth noting that you have certain time in which to do each level and when the timer hits zero Death (A grim reaper) will chase you and if he catches you means it is game over. To counter this, each human save adds one minute to the timer.
You also have health points in the game, you start each level with a certain amount of hearts. You lose health points by being close to a fire which will increase the fire intensity (Pointed to you in a red bar in the middle of the screen around your character). If this is full you will lose a health point. The fires also shoot fireballs which you have to extinguish. Once you run out of health, this means game over.
When extinguishing fires, saving people and cats you get money. You can use this money on skills such as getting discounts on them, being able to hold more water and more time. This is fun as they assist quite a bit.
I started in the game using a controller. The controls were well laid out and I didn't find it too hard to gain mastery over the placement of the buttons. Likewise with the Keyboard, a WASD movement combined with left click for water and right click for foam. F button was interact and Z was for talking to people. It's worth noting however that you can change the button schemes in the main menu which means you have a lot of flexibility with them. The characters movements are easy to control and you won't have no difficulty navigating around.
When you start each level it begins with a very smooth and fun cut scene. Out of all my time playing the game, I have never completed a mission. Embarrassingly enough it's because of my skill level. so I cannot say if the story goes deeper or if there are special cut scenes for completing missions.
The graphics of the game are very peculiar, The are cartoonish and colourful. Almost like Blazes moustache. All the graphics were solid though, there were no glitches or any bad side effects from much action. They all worked like they should have.
The music was composed especially for the game by Rimsky Music in Barcelona. The main song of the track seems to be everywhere and loops over and over. I do like it though but after a while had to turn it off.  All the other sound effects like the fire burning and the people talking were fine and added well to the whole experience.
I personally would've preferred if there were difficulty settings as the game for me is really difficult. I do enjoy the challenge but would've loved to been able to spend longer on the levels without the fear of Death grabbing me. Other than that, I really did enjoy the game and the whole fire fighting experience as a whole. This is definitely for the more die hard gamers who enjoy a tough challenge. If you're looking for an easy task then fire fighting is definitely not easy!
The bottom line is that I would recommend this game, it's fun, challenging and very rewarding!
Edit: I did learn how to play the game better and got real far, which was a real fun experience for me. Unfortunately, I got too far ahead of myself and started rushing. Once I opened the door which I forgot to extinguish first, I ended up inevitably dying from back draft. :)

Helldivers is a game with a great concept and very fluid, well-executed mechanics. Your first jumps really make you feel like a badass, and the emphasis on teamwork to pull you through incredibly hectic missions is just awesome. The weapons feel great to use, the methods to accomplish objectives feel very interactive and hectic as you're being assaulted on all sides, the stealth mechanic in eliminating enemy patrols before they can sound an alarm gives you good variance to how missions can go. The shared galactic campaign is pretty neat too, with all players' efforts in various helldives resulting in points toward campaign objective completion (rewarded more influence in the campaign for harder dives than easier ones).
The only thing that really holds back this game on PC right now -- and it really does -- is the matchmaking. It is utterly atrocious. Sometimes you'll only see 2 games to join in the matchmaking list (even if you don't have a planet selected and it should include everyone from your region). Most of the time you won't be able to join on anybody you select -- at least it has been true for me that connections to the great majority of games in the matchmaking list fail, and I often spend just as much time trying to get into a squad with someone as I do actually playing. Not to mention that you can often drop connections right after missions are complete so you don't remain in multiplayer for the next mission either and have to find a NEW squad to join in on. No other game I play comes close to networking and matchmaking problems this poor. When it does work, it's -- again -- pretty great. This is a really neat game, and I was close to recommending it anyway, but even at $20 I just cannot honestly recommend it until the horrific matchmaking issues are completely solved.

Okay, to be honest, I'm a little torn on how to feel about this game.  It's an otome/dating sim game as the title suggests, you play as a high school student whose grandfather passes away and are given his estate in his will.  Your father who is a **** pretty much forces you to go live in it on the excuse that it will be good for you to get used to living there but really he's just a **** who doesn't want to listen to you.  You find that when you get there there are five cute demon boys bleeding and passed out on your floor for reasons unknown.  Eventually they end up living there with you for a while until they can defeat the devil, Malix, who did this to them and who was running rampant in your city.  Just to give a short gist.
You can date any of the five icubi brothers as you may assume, your two friends Suzu and Naomi, a boy named Andrew, and even one of the "villains" of the game as well.  So six male love interests and three female.  Unfortunately while you may think that the brothers are the most interesting options aside from the villain in question, they're not.  That's one thing that makes this game kind of fall flat for me.  The routes for the boys are very cookie cutter in nature, they are almost exactly the same just with their names inserted into prewritten paragraphs with a few occasional changes here and there for the most part.  Their "unique" scenes are pretty much the same with just name changes.  I wish that they had different scenes instead of the same scenes rehashed with a few changes.  While there are some scenes that are quite different such as the one where Diana appears in your house at one point they still are kind of the same in nature.  And I somehow found that I enjoyed the human love interests more than most of the incubi boys.
Another issue that arises is that this game is very, very short.  The game takes place over the course of one week.  Which I feel is a little ridiculous.  Even if the main love interests are incubi and there's that whole ~*~DEMON MAGIC~*~ element going on, it's very unrealistic.  I wish that there was more time in between events rather than happening immediately after they were eluded to.  Or at the very least I wish there are some little moments of respite in between each day like where you could visit the boys in their rooms and talk to them or go out or just SOMETHING.
Now, onto my issue with the games writing.  While I did kind of cover this before in saying that many of the routes are almost exactly the same with a few changes here and there for the incubi boys routes, that's not my main issue.  The writing feels very unprofessional at points.  Namely at points where characters are shouting, especially the protagonist in one of the first scenes.  There are excessive uses of exclamation points and question marks to the point where it just looks kind of dumb, to be perfectly honest, and I have played a ton of old RPGs like Suikoden that use a ton of these, but usually no more than four or five per sentence.  The scene I pointed out in particular uses at least ten for one sentence and there are about five or more sentences in that dialogue box.  It is ridiculous.  This isn't the only time this happens either.  Perhaps it's just me but it really bothers me to see dialogue like that.  Also the dialogue options (the very few times they actually appear...) are kind of written in a silly manner a lot of the time and I feel they just don't fit.  Again, this may just be me who has an issue with this, but as I said about the excessive exclamation points and question marks, it just looks very odd and unnecessary.  The dialogue options also seldom make you feel like you've done much of anything.  There are also typos every now and again in the game.  Which I am willing to let slide as they do tend to happen in text heavy games.
Now, we will move onto the art and voice acting.  I enjoyed the voice acting a lot, some people in other reviews seem not to and I can understand why, but I've never been too picky with that sort of thing and I think that most of them at least are very good and have potential.  The art on the other hand while I do like it, I have some issues with it.  Mostly in the CGs.  The style of the CGs and character portraits are drastically different.  To the point where I wonder if it was two different artists who did them.  The lines are very thick and black on the CGs compared to the portraits and at times the anatomy is a little...well, it could use some work.  Characters also don't exactly look like themselves sometimes.  There is also something weird that happens past a certain point, where the protagonists portrait in the lower left of the dialogue box just...disappears.  And never comes back.  It's really odd.  Not sure if that was done on purpose or just an accident, but yeah, that's a thing.
To end things off, I enjoyed the game for the most part, especially the first time through, I liked it a lot when I first played.  But upon my second playthrough on another boys route, I suddenly felt...a little cheated I guess?  Because of how cookie cutter the other routes were.  I also found that I enjoyed the routes of characters who were not the main focus of the game more than I probably should have which is kind of disappointing and I don't think should have been an intended thing to happen.  I think that the writer was kind of lazy in how they did certain things, with how short the game really is I think the least they could have done was not reuse text for the boys "unique" scenes in their routes.  It feels very lazy and was what took my enjoyment away from the game the second time through.  It was disappointing.  It also made me feel that replaying to see the other boys endings was kind of pointless.  I think the worst part is that the boys are all unique in and of themselves so they had a lot of potential to work with, but they just got stuck with well, generic prewritten dialogue with their names tacked on for the most part.  If you don't mind that sort of thing though, this shouldn't bother you.  If you're like me and it does just play one boys route who you really like and then just play the other options that aren't the main boys.  It will probably be more enjoyable that way.  I will give this a positive review, but mostly because I cannot give a neutral one.  The game is also worth giving a shot mostly because for one it is indeed free and if you like dating sims a lot it may still be something you might enjoy at least on the first time through.  I'd probably give it a six or seven out of ten.
Pros:
Enjoyable on your first playthrough.
Voice acting is rather nice for the most part.
Music is also very good.
Art is nice for the most part, aside from some small things which shouldn't bother most people.
The game's format is pretty simple so if you've never played a dating sim game before it should be easy for you to jump onto.
There are several endings to go for.
It's free.
Cons:
Consecutive playthroughs can feel rather dull and unenjoyable due to how cookie cutter the majority of the routes are in nature.
Writing can appear unprofessional at points due to excessive uses of punctuation, caps lock, and just oddly phrased dialogue options.
On the note of dialogue options they are very few and far between and the majority of them make you feel like you've done little to change anything at all.
Some aspects of the art may bother you, but it all depends on how much of a stickler you are for such things.
The plot of the game can be extremely generic in places, such as how your "rival" (who rarely appears) is blonde and has blue eyes and is just so rude and mean to you but is somehow the most popular girl in school.
The game is extremely short taking place over the course of about a week.

Seduce me is a dating sim that definitely exceeds what I expected to get for free. Fully voiced with 9 romance routes and several more endings, it definitely warrants a playthrough. It lists trigger warnings at the very beginning of the game which is good, though if it were a paid game I would prefer them on the steam page so you could see before buying, But despite the trigger warnings being pretty heavy, I have not yet seen much of them in the content of the game (keep in mind I have only played 3/9 routes). For example one of the tws listed is abuse, but all I've really seen of that in game so far is your father slaps you once (which isnt played lightly) and possibly that a character acts in a way he doesn't really want to please his mother (though i dont think he would be in any danger if he didnt). For a game literally about 'sex demons' the focus on consent is very refreshing.
It took me about 3-4 hours to get through the first route. The story is pretty simple, but as you go through different choices and routes you get to see more and of the reason behind why things happened the way they did. The voice acting for many characters is very good, and really adds to the experience. The addition of both Girl/Girl and Girl/Boy romances is welcome, even if none of the five 'main' love interests is female. The biggest drawback is the main incubi routes are largely the same, but for the low price of free its not really something to complain about. With the level of content this game had I wouldn't have minded paying 2-5 euros for it.

Half-Life 2: Episode One is science fiction first person shooter game developed by Valve Software on the Source Engine. It tells the continued story of physicist-gone-action-hero Gordon Freeman as he and action-hero-gone-love-interest Alyx Vance escape from the physically unstable City 17 before it blows up I think.
In my review of Half-Life 2 I definitely wasn't very nice to the game. I said the game was unfocused and average, with interesting ideas and clever storytelling but drawn-out setpeices and a largely uninteresting plot if you remove all that glittery facial animation. Some of that, I think, is still justified but one thing I forgot to mention was how much I actually really like Half-Life 2.
One thing the HL franchise enjoys doing is pulling the rug out from under the player and then throwing a bunch of enemies at them. That's pretty cool but it's also sort of troubling, considering that most of Half-Life 2 feels very aimless as if Gordon is just drunkenly stumbling between ambushes and set-peices. Episode 1 seemingly tries to fix that by making whatever the current goal is very obvious, either with some kind of environmental clue or with Alyx directly telling you what the objective is:
Escape the tower
Get to the train station
The story is more grounded and because of that the gameplay can throw you into as many accidental circumstances and detours as it wants because you always end up back on track.
I also appreciate how the stakes are a lot higher feeling in this game. It isn't just a vague intergalactic business proposition between Breen and some alien terrorist people, the actual city feels like it's about to blow up and if you keep getting interrupted by the combine than everybody involved will actually die. And it isn't just your life that's at stake here, you spend the entire game fighting alongside Alyx Vance, which sounds like a bad idea but this game manages a sidekick-idea very well.
Anybody who played the first game remembers the third act where you command a squad consisting of that guy who sounds like everyone else and a girl who only occasionally dreams of cheese(?) but nobody WANTS to remember that part because not only is it sandwiched between the two best parts of the game but it also is un-doubtably the worst. The AI blocks the player at every turn and is super reliant on Gordon; they will not go anywhere unless you ask them too and they die as quickly as your enemies do so they may as well not be there--heck the game is more fun when they AREN'T there.
The squad idea comes back in Episode 1 but not only are they more resistant, they seemingly abandon the whole "Targeting" thing--they seem to go wherever they want until you start to progress, and most importantly they stay out of the players way. All of this culminates into Alyx who not only follows the player from the very start but is INVULNERABLE to damage. This could make her too powerful but the devs fix that only giving her a pistol until about halfway through, and even before that she's a very good aim. Most of the opening is spent with the player under a variety of handicaps such as only having a gravity gun or not having a ton of ammo and the devs cleverly use Alyx as your second half, which not only ties their mostly plot-based comradery into the gameplay but also makes you feel like a real team by the end.
Ultimately I think Episode 1 expands on HL2 and makes the game better. There's only one new enemy and a smaller arsenal than before but the gameplay is tightened and the story in more investing. I'll be the first to admit that my review of HL2 was a bit hyperbolic but I still recommended that game and I absolutely recommend Episode 1 as well

TLDR:  This game had so much potential. Unfortunately, I felt let down at the end. Only buy if it's on sale.
Pros:
-Fun, challenging first-person 3D puzzle platformer.
-No "training wheels." This is a subjective pro/con, but I thoroughly enjoyed the fact that this game simply introduces mechanics then throws you to the wolves, making you use your head (and much trial and error) to solve some of the puzzles.
-Setting and environment is amazing in this game. The various levels feel alien, yet vaguely familiar.
-The introduction and setup to the story was amazing and very poignant. I'll get to the rest of the plot in the cons section.
Cons:
-EXTREMELY short game. I finished my entire first playthrough in just over two hours, and I have archived stream footage to prove it.
-Horrendous voice acting. I've heard better speakers at third-grade Thanksgiving plays.
-Character models are sub-par by most standards.
-Taking the last two points into consideration, I feel as if the devs concentrated all their effort on level design and completely ignored the characters. Which is a shame, because the story suffers greatly from flat, boring characters, visually and vocally.
-Back to the plot: it starts off very well, and just gets increasingly worse from there. I know many people writing reviews about this game loved the plot, but honestly I found it mostly un-authentic and cheesy.
Conclusion:
A Story About My Uncle tried to be the next Portal or The Talos Principle, and it got half-way there. The game did have some very fun, challenging puzzles and great, atmospheric level designs. However, it missed the heart and soul that a good game should have. The devs didn't spend enough time on the plot and on the characters, and the result was a game that had a short, cheesy plot with an abrupt ending, and flat, boring characters. I recommend this game, but only barely. Only buy if you can find it on sale, because it's definitely not worth its current price of $13.

Aiming while moving can be hard though. I can't count how many times I missed my grapples and fell into the misty abyss. But I usually didn't mind. It just meant it was time to go soaring again. After two or three seconds of freefall it resets you to your last checkpoint, which is generally right at a ledge, so downtime is very short. You can even charge your jump before the reset. This is an unusual time for the race of vampires, as hideous murders, rampant bloodletting among the human population, and medieval vampire-hunters are beginning to make it very difficult for vampires to remain California's dark secret.

Excellent top-down shooter with a fast pace, good community, and fun style that is lighthearted but also can be quite intense and challenging. It plays very similar to Alien Swarm, but with some of the key-combo magic present in Magicka and Gauntlet, both made by this same team (and both quite good as well).
A variety of playstyles work: standard assault weapons/shotguns, futuristic lasers, vehicles, loading up on airstrikes... and of course combinations of any and all of those with teammates. 40 hours in I'm still learning a lot of new ways to play and still have a lot of gear I want to upgrade with the unlock points you steadily earn.
You can play solo, but for harder difficulties multiplayer is more effective and fun. Matchmaking is easy and the community players are very cooperative.
DLC note:
Buy the Digital Deluxe Edition, it's the cheapest way to get all the DLC and you can't unlock the DLC weapons/gear any other way. Although you can complete all missions without it, it adds variety and more ways to strategize and progression choices for spending points.

As a technology showcase for the Unreal engine this game does a fine job as it is exceedingly pretty and fabulously detailed even on modest hardware; but as an enjoyable narriative experience it's singularly lacking.
It starts off on the wrong foot by boldly proclaiming "This game is a narrative experience that does not hold your hand." What exactly is the purpose of this? Is it a dig at other games? An attempted disclaimer against this sort of criticism? Are they not confident that the nature of the game will become readily apparent through playing it? It's up to the gamer to decide what the experience means to them, so stating "this is a narrative experience" comes across as somewhat presumptuous.
Also, what's wrong with a linear narrative? That's how narratives have worked for countless ages -- you're taken through them by some other agency. Whether you're listening to a story, reading a book or watching a film, you are led through the narrative. The interactive nature of games opens up unprecedented opportunities for non-linear storytelling, but that doesn't mean there's anything wrong with the old sort.
Anyway, the game. It opens up in a pretty, forested, mountainous and remote setting. Right away there are creepy traps and a gristly murder scene, which sets the scene as a sort of less-subtle Stephen King knockoff. There's an obvious puzzle - as in, something that is obviously a puzzle - and yet it became quickly obvious that solving it was optional, and that one could press ahead if one so wished.
A sinking feeling that this was the narrative-delivery mechanism made me stick around to try and solve it, because I knew that I wasn't going to want to come back. One of the things you need to find is a small rock. Your unspecified spidey-sense does not help with the location of gameplay objects. The environment is filled with rocks. After a few minutes another sinking feeling that locating hard-to-find objects played a big part in this prompted me to a walkthrough, which disappointingly confirmed my suspicions on both counts. After moving the tiny rock a few yards, you then have to reassemble some fragments of a cutscene into the right order, so that the cutscene will play, something which serves no purpose other than wasting time.
Not holding your hand though a narrative is one thing, but denying you that narrative until you jump through the relevant arbitrary puzzle hoops is unforgivable. A well designed puzzle is one which you feel that you *want* to solve for no reason other than to solve it. When you can see what you have to do but don't want to do it -- that is a poorly designed puzzle.
The narrative segment itself was largely implausible, as those which centre around killing someone by running them over with a train tend to be.
Each 'section' follows the same basic premise; there's been a horrible moider, you need to find a specific object, move it a few yards, use your spidey sense and then assemble the pieces of a cutscene. One of the sections features a completely out-of-place jump scare (which does nothing other than to push you back to the start of a maze section and destroy and immersion which you may have managed to accumulate) and then cumulates in the sort of symbol arranging pseudopuzzle that at least had the good grace to always have the same solution so that the walkthrough screenshot would solve it.
The story was working towards a fairly generic sleeping-horror-must-not-be-woken kind of deal but I quite like those so stuck with it; but then at the last moment it faked out with an epically lame twist, and the credits left me feeling profoundly disenfranchised -- and that is the sole reason for my 'not recommended' review; it left me feeling like I'd wasted my time playing it.

Another FREE dating sim on steam!
Pros:
-The heroine is a smart girl who can come to inherit her grandfather's company. She doesn't expect anyone to save her but isn't afraid to admit she needs help either. She's also very booksmart, knows Taekwondo and is overall relatable.
-The game isn't soley about romance. It's got a lot of story to it related to the love interests personalities and family struggles, getting the heroine involved in their lives, putting her in danger and BEING LOGICAL ABOUT IT. We also see the heroine deal with her past and the loss of her grandfather, who she was obviously very close to and her possibly inheriting his company and what she wants to do with her future.
-I feel the romance actually ENHANCES the story rather than it being a requirement or an optional goal. It ends up being something you want to pursue to see where the story goes.
-There is too much story to explain in one review...
-The Heroine's friends actually serve a purpose unlike most dating sims where the best friend character is either encouraging or forcing the hero to date or hook up with people. They're also GxG options!
-The 5 demon characters are very nice characters, each of them is distinct and they don't sexually harass or abuse the heroine in a way that's offensive or borderline♥♥♥♥♥♥(unlike a few other otomes such as Diabolik Lovers and definately unlike 'literature' such as Twighlight or 50 Shades of Grey). They feel like very human characters despite the fact they're demons. They're also very human i that, i can see a real person acting the way some of these characters do. Their love for the heroine also feels genuine. And the fact they treat her with so much respect even when first meeting her is also something i appreciate about this game, especially since so many other books and games about dating a supernatural being can get so creepy when it comes to the romance aspect...
-The voicework is pretty good. I didn't expect a free game like this to be voiced.
-The music tends to loop, but it does set the mood for the scenes where the music is played
-There are straight and lesbian options for the female heroine to choose from (i even made a guide for one of the lesbian options)
- A few months after it's release, THEY ADDED ACHIEVEMENTS TO HELP YOU KEEP TRACK OF YOUR LOVE MAKING!
-IT'S FREE!
Cons:
- No Harem ending (seriously? You have 5 incubi... How could you not have a harem route with INCUBI BEING THE MAIN LOVE INTERESTS?!).
-The screenshots on the store page can be a little misleading. Those screenshots DO appear in-game but that's no the art style you'll always be seeing. The art style in-game can be a bit narmy and goofy to look at first time around, but it could be worse and it's not all that bad once you get used to the style. It's a bit rough around the edges but also very charming as well. And the game is free! It would be worse if they charged money for worse art or no art at all.
-The way you meet the demons and the antagonists are a bit typical at best, but because the 5 main demon characters are so human in their actions and behaviors, i honestly don't mind. The villains are typical but they also have somewhat of a charm too (notably Diana).
-Speaking of Villians and anatagonists though, only Diana is a possible love interest and only she gets some spotlight. The villians the 5 demon boys fight against is a Devil named Malix but his so called 'arc' is extremely short lived. It kind of makes me wonder if it was supposed to be longer and maybe the creator ran out of time, money or other resources? It's a shame as it feels extremely short lived, somewhat random and it could've had a lot more potential and possibly added 2 more love interests to the game and a variety of more endings. As a writer myself, i really get ticked off at wasted potential! I originally thought the Malix 'arc' was going to span a longer period of time, at least enough time where you could get to know each of the brothers, maybe help them train for their next fight with him.
-No trading cards or badges, which is also kind of a shame because i would LOVE backgrounds and emotes of the characters.
-My biggest con aside from the Malix 'arc' is that the game can feel extremely short. Most dating sims give you a good amount of time to get to know each of the love interests and maybe even some free time to interact with other characters who don't have routes of their own depending on the game or if the game is more 'visual novel' than 'dating sim' and vice versa. Sadly you really only get to interact with 1 of the demon boys per playthrough or not interact with them at all... We do get to see their backstories in the short amount of gameplay but because so many other dating sims give us more time to get to know their characters, it's a real shame Seduce Me didn't give us more time to know more than just 1 brother per playthrough! I expected to spend weeks or months with these characters (in a similar fashion to Persona 4 or Hatoful Boyfriend where dates can be skipped or looked over for the sake of keeping the story a good legnth), but instead we only spend about 2 days or so with them, which is FULL OF LOST POTENTIAL!
All in all, similar to my review of Everlasting Summer, there isn't any reason you shouldn't try this game out at least once. It's free so there's no risk in trying it out and it's very different from other dating sims i've played on steam or otherwise. Both of them have intellegent heroes that you control throughout the story and loveable love interests that you can easily get attached to and friendly with if love isn't what you're aiming for. However, this game can be very short and unlike other dating sims i've seen on Steam, you can only get an oppertunity to romance 1 character per playthrough. In addition there is a lot of lost story potential when it comes to the Malix 'arc', lost potential for character development because you can only romance 1 character per playthrough, lost potential for non-romance routes
, lost potential in exploring your options because the game play is so short, lost potential in exploring your options because you pretty much have to interact with the demons or not interact with them at all, and wasn't interacting with them kind of the point? There's too much lost potential to explain in one review... Which saddens me as a writer to no end.
Despite the lost potential and short legnth however, I absolutely LOVE Seduce Me because of the choices it made with the characters (like not making the heroine an airhead, not making the supernatural love interests creepy and/or abusive toward her, having the heroine's friends have an actual purpose in the story unlike most dating sims, ect!).
All in all, i give this game 3.8 Spies saying 'Seduce me' out of 5

The Witcher is an action role-playing hack and slash video game developed by CD Projekt RED and published by Atari.
The game is based on the book series of the same name by Polish author Andrzej Sapkowski. The Witcher takes place in a medieval fantasy world and follows the story of Geralt, one of a few remaining "witchers" – traveling monster hunters for hire, gifted with unnatural powers. The game's system of "moral choices" as part of the storyline was noted for its time-delayed consequences and lack of black-and-white morality.
The game utilises BioWare's proprietary Aurora Engine. A console version using an entirely new engine and combat system, titled The Witcher: Rise of the White Wolf, was to be released in Autumn 2009 but was suspended due to payment problems with the console developers, Widescreen Games.
On September 18, 2009, CD Projekt RED officially confirmed that they began working on a sequel, The Witcher 2: Assassins of Kings, which was released on May 17, 2011 for the PC and on 17 April 2012, for Xbox 360. The third game of the series, titled The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, was released on May 18, 2015.

This is a fun game. I'm bad at giving things numeric ratings, so I'll just go over my thoughts on the most likely reason people wouldn't want to buy this game. For the most part they're pulled from the negative reviews (which are all relatively ostracized and 'unhelpful', suggesting these people are in the vast minority. Then again, that's also because a lot of them are quite ineloquent).
So without further ado, things people may gripe about related to buying/playing this game:
"The game is too short"
It took me about 1.5 hours to beat the game without caring about taking damage or getting a good score on normal. If you don't care about beating it on hard or if your motto is 'D stands for Diploma' then chances are you may think the game is 'too short' although I'd argue that it's still a better time/money ratio than going to a movie.
"All you do is click on things"
This is something of a 2D-action beat-em-up where you jump around, enemies show up, and sometimes (but not always) you have to kill a certain number of enemies before being able to scroll the screen. A key mechanic is that, if you're hovering over an enemy, clicking the mouse will jump/drag/move your character to the enemy. That in combination with the fact that rapid-clicking will result in pretty quick basic attacks that will destroy most normal enemies.
This is not to say that you still don't have to move left and right. Add to that the fact that ducking is also required on more than one occasion, means that anyone who says 'all you have to do is click on things' is clearly exagerating, which is one of the reasons why no-one likes them (er, 'finds them helpful').
In reality, you have 4 keys for move/jump/duck and can perform special moves by double clicking up/left/right or holding the right mouse button and swiping. Aside from further invalidating the afforementioned argument, this also provides a fun way to move faster than walking/jumping speed, which is always welcomed.
Basically, yes, on normal you COULD beat MOST of the game with only the right arrow and the left mouse button, but I wouldn't recommend it. If you're never using specials then, well, I don't know why you would do that.
"It's too easy"
*shrug* I'll admit, I didn't die that much on normal and I didn't spend too much time paying attention to boss patterns or trying to avoid hits or etc. That being said, I did die a few times and I got the lowest letter ranking on every level. Getting an A (I assume? maybe higher?) rank would, probably, take at least some effort to achieve. Also, I tried to play level 1 with the same carefree attitude on hard and managed to die without too much trouble, but I probably wouldn't have if I would have been taking it slower.
"It's boring"
Watch the trailer. That's the game. If you think that's boring then don't buy the game. Not every game is for everyone, but I seriously don't understand this argument once you see what you're getting yourself in to.
"The art style is [insert criticism]"
*Shrug* I think it's fine, but my first system was a Genesis so I'm no stranger to pixels. I think the art in the game is great, but I wasn't playing full screen. Really though, just see the above comment and replace 'that's boring' with 'that represents a sub-par art-style' and I think we're good.
"Rawr I made a complaint about the game and you didn't include mine, I hate you"
Um... my bad, maybe your complaint should be more logical ;-). If you think your complaint is logical, please just leave a comment or, y'know, don't bother me and go away :-D.

A Story About My Uncle, while $12.99, is well-worth the money. (More so if you get it while it's on sale.)
It's a short, sweet story. You are the father, and your daughter wants to be told a bedtime story. You decide to tell her about your uncle, Fred, and how you followed him into a strange world for an adventure, after Fred had been gone for some time. You find a suit he had made to fit you just right, but never got around to asking you to come on an adventure with him, as he had stayed on his latest adventure for a good while, which is what prompts you to go find him.
You meet this species of frog people, later revealed to have been created by your uncle, who accidentally sent them to the world, and that is why he went on an adventure; to retrieve them back, but by the time he had gotten there to collect them, they had already grown. You meet a girl name Madeline (Maddie). She joins you for a while to help find your uncle Fred. She accompanies you for a time, until you find the 'Strays' which were people who originally lived in the village of the frog people, but moved out of the dark, damp caves and moved to a place called 'Star Haven' and created a new, prosperous village. Once you arrive in Star Haven, Maddie decides she wants to stay there with the Strays, and wishes you luck on finding your uncle, but she has one last request; If you do find him, have him go back to visit Maddie in Star Haven.
Jump forward a bit, after going through the trecherous Ice Caves, at the end of the final tunnel, you find your Uncle Fred and some of his equipment laying around. He hears the footsteps, and turns around calling out "Hello?" to which he is surprised to see you. He comments on how you're wearing his suit, and asks what you're doing there. You comment on how you found it in his Workshop, and came to look for him.
Unfortunately, your Uncle wanted you to go back home. You reluctantly agree after wanting to stay there with your Uncle Fred and Maddie, but your uncle insists you go back to the real world and find your adventure there. You step on the pad, and your uncle activates it, which launches you back to your world, out of the cave full of crystals. That was the end of the bedtime story for your daughter.
While you don't know what happened to your uncle, you know no matter what, hes on his biggest adventure yet. You go back after telling your daughter your story back to your uncle's house. Things are packed up, cleaned up. There's also a small memorial with a picture of your uncle, who has not returned from his adventure since you came back. You came back every day, ocassionally remembering your uncle's voice asking for you to get him this or that tool. Unfortunately the closet where your suit was is locked up tight, and you can't get in it. You head upstairs to the Observatory one last time to find the pad that originally sent you there presumably still there, but not funcional and covered in snow from the open window.

Quick Reference:
THE GOOD
• Immersive and interesting story.
• Good character development.
• Gorgeous world with excelent graphics.
• Good and fitting soundtrack.
• Nice voice-acting.
THE BAD
• Weird auto-save system.
• The game does not hold your hand, so it's easy to miss things or to get lost in the world.
SPECIAL (These are topics that are too long to be in a quick reference. If you wanna read about them, go to the end of the review. There will be No Spoilers, I promise.)
• The ending
• Hours worth of game.
Throught review and commentary:
> IMMERSIVE AND INTERESTING STORY
Immersion is definetely the strongest point of this game. The graphics and the way the story is told and the lack of  HUD make the immersion easy and enjoyable. With no HUD, there is nothing or almost nothing to distract you from the experience of playing. It's easy to fell in the shoes of Paul Prospero and the story is pretty good. You feel the need to find out what is happening, why it's happening and how things came to be the way they are. The game is a narrative experience, so this is, as it should be, it's strongest point.
> GOOD CHARACTER DEVELOPMENT
There is only a handful of characters in the story and you don't get to see them all that much, but you can clearly distinct each one of them by their personalities. The best of all, though, is not how the characters are, but how they are portrayed in some elements of the game. But I won't spoil it for you. You'll understand when(hopefully) you play the game and think hard enough about it. Have fun!
> GORGEOUS WORLD WITH EXCELLENT GRAPHICS
This is part of what makes the immersion so good. This is one of (if not the) most beautiful games I've ever played. I've found myself stopping to watch some landscapes. This made me thank myself for investing money in a great computer.
> GOOD AND FITTING SOUNDTRACK.
The sounds can really make you feel the game. Also part of the great immersion. THIS IS A GAME TO BE PLAYED ON HEADPHONES(or really loud speakers, if you and the people around you have no problem with it.) The music can make you feel relaxed, anxious, sad... Well, it does it's job well.
> NICE VOICE ACTING
Unique voices and acting won't allow you to mistake a character for another. The actors did a really good job on making each character distinguishable, even when you can only hear and not see them.
X WEIRD AUTO-SAVE SYSTEM
Well, you don't only have to learn the game here, you'll also want to learn how the auto-save system works. You will eventually feel like you can't leave play whenever you want. It is not a big issue, really. But it is something I thought was worth to mention.
X THE GAME DOES NOT HOLD YOUR HAND
The game itself says: "This is a narrative experience that does not hold your hand." This is the first thing you get to read in the whole game, even before the intro. Well, this is an open-world game with mysteries scaterred around. It is very easy to completely miss something. I got stuck two or three times. Well, it can happen. It is not an easy game.
>> CONCLUSION <<
One of the best experiences I've ever had with a game in my life. No wonder I came here to write such a detailed review. This is a very well-crafted game that is all about the experience of playing it. If I were to give you a piece of advice: Play this game in a moment people do not need you, or won't call you. As I said, this game is all about the immersion, and being interrupted breaks it, so try not to let yourself be interrupted.
That said, I believe this game is worth it's full price. And I do recomend you to buy it and hope you enjoy it as much as I did. Cheers!
** THE ENDING
When you clear the game you will remember what I'm saying here: THERE IS MORE THAN MEETS THE EYE.
It is very easy to see what the ending looks like judge on the spot. People seem to do this frequently when there is SO MUCH MORE to it. When you clear this game, give the ending, and the whole story, a second thought, or research about it. You won't regret it. I promise.
** HOURS WORTH OF GAME
This is not a long game on it's own. And replaying The Vanishing of Ethan Carter is just like re-reading a book. You will go through the same scenes again. Well, you might pick some pieces of the story you didn't get right the first time, but there is nothing completely new. Looking at it that way it seems like a short lived game. But again: There is more than meets the eye. Try to give things a second thought, rethink the game and you might find many hours of fun without being actually playing.

Great game to experience, despite its shortcomings.
The ASCII theming is beautiful, and well executed in conjunction with the soundtrack.
There is a lot of fine details and complexities built in to the racial/class selection options. Despite all of them having incredibly similar skillsets, all of their nuances lead to significantly different playstyles.
There are so many different options in combat that result in some complex tactical decisions. With the exception of a few mildly brainless builds or if you significantly overwhelm your opponent, rolling over the same combos against each opponent will not work. There are several probability based status effects or opponent skills that you will need to actively respond to or face the consequences.
Now for my biggest gripe. I am a big fan of the rogue-like and rogue-lite genres. Death can be fun, death is a learning experience, etc. However, it's all relative to the amount of grind that it took to take you up to that death. The first dozen hours or so of SanctuaryRPG are full of so many learning opportunities, that all those many hours spent fighting and crafting weren't a grind at all. But after that point, death becomes frustratingly expensive, because of how many dozens of hours the game can span. This in turn, actually encourages even more grind to the point of getting your character over-leveled for a particular area, as a safety barrier to protect from dying all over again. And there will come fights that completely blindside you from where you completely overwhelmed the previous fight, so there's very little available to signal danger to you until it is far too late.
All that said, though, despite my frustrations with the circumstances surrounding death, learning how to play and experiencing SanctuaryRPG for the first time was a great experience, and frankly a steal at $8.

If ever there were a love letter written to 1990's era Treasure, Noitu Love 2 is it. Frantic, fast, furious, and fun. It can take a bit to come to grips with the unique control scheme, but once you've spent some time in the tutorial and gotten mastery of a few stages under your belt, you'll be up to speed and zip around the screen causing all manners of chaos.
The game features an incredible amount of variety packed into its arcade length. There's no shortage of stage gimmicks and unique fodder enemies to pound away on, and how could you forget the positively over-the-top boss encounters, which will push your dexterity to the limit and require a good bit of thought to truly best.
Noitu Love's difficulty is also balanced very well. Each of the game's difficulties suits a range of player skill levels, and advancing to a higher difficulty level doesn't only make enemies hit harder, they also have a few new tricks up their sleeve which keep things fresh and interesting. It's far from punishing like a lot of 2D platformers and action games these days tend to be, but you will be tested and failure only leads to more learning.
Add a couple unlockable playable characters with some fun stage variations between them on top and you've got an amazingly solid little package just eager for lovers of frantic old-school games to take hold of and enjoy.
When this game isn't crashing, it's a pretty good time.

To preface this, I played The Room One as well and they kept a lot of the same problems as well as were able to fix some problems. Also this game is pretty cheap so many of the problems can be overlooked.
CONS:
However, there are many cons to this game. The most frustrating is the controls. Be it as simple as they are, small things like double clicking to zoom and right clicking to back out gets really annoying really fast. Since it is very difficult to tell what way to turn handles, what you can pick up, or where you CAN zoom in, you will just be clicking wildly on the screen until something works with something. That isnt a puzzle, thats just elongated gameplay. It leads to extreme frustration which for me just meant that i could only do a chapter per sitting without having to turn the game off.
I love puzzle escape games, but what sets them apart is when the puzzles are fun since you can easily tell what you can use, and the real puzzle is what to do with what you are given. This game is just clicking and dragging until something fits in a really linear way. Thats not fun, thats work. For example you could be zoomed into a box and know that a key goes there so you drag the item from your inventory. But it doesn't work. The place was right, the shape was right, but you weren't zoomed in enough. your face has to be inches from the device to work. Or when you open a cabenet but the view is so zoomed in that the door wont open if you drag it across the screen, so you back up. But you cant touch the handle one step back. Nitpicking, but that is the entirety of the short game.
PROS:
The Room Two made many good improvements over the first game. Such as the room design no longer being just a box in a room, now its a whole room to 'explore' with themes and items besides boxes. The atmostphere is amped up many notches wich is something the game didn't need but highly benefits from. Cutscenes are better, lighting is better, graphics are better, length is better.
The best improvement in my opion though is the atmosphere. This isnt a horror game by any means but i have had many instances of pulling away from the screen in fear as a noise echoes from the darkenss. Any time the lens is put on i expect to see spine shivering video footage as i did in only one occasion in The Room. This works really well with the creepy but calm ambiance that suddenly switches to something sinister. If you want a good scare i recomend playing this in the dark of night alone with headphones, though its definetly not Amnesia level scares.
RATING:
I'm not a professional critic so I'm not going to give it a number score, but i will say that I can recomend this game for the price. If its on sale, then I'd pick it up right away. It's rare to find good uneasy 'horror' games on steam for this much. If mindlessly clicking isn't really your thing, then don't waste your time.

Some of the puzzles were a bit unintuitive or dull but overall it was a lot of fun, atmospheric and aesthetically enchanting, like playing with an antique puzzle box. Has some jump scares but it's not a scary game overall, just spooky. Plot didn't make a bunch of sense to me but that's not why you play these games :)

Let's get a few things out of the way first. I'm not sure whether to recommend this game or not, but I can recognise the developers created something extraordinary here, and that at least deserved being mentioned.
This game is basically a walking simulator, but unlike for example The Stanley Parable, there are no alternate routes or endings. Replayability is non-existent here. Depending on how leisurely you play and how fast you resort to walkthroughs, you'll get about two to five hours out of this 'game'. In that sense you're probably thinking this game is overpriced, and I agree.
I won't go into too much detail about the story, as that really is the meat of the game. I don't want to take away from that. But essentially, you are Paul Prospero, a detective with a keen eye for the supernatural, and you have come to Red Creek Valley per request of Ethan Carter's fanmail. As you solve murders and puzzles, the overarching plot reveals itself to you through cutscenes and voice-overs.
The way this works is you are dropped into a gorgeous, sprawling open-world with the clues scattered about. This is very reminiscent of point-and-click games, but the difference is you can actually (un)intentionally skip puzzles or scenes and walk further into the world. But to get the ending, you'll have to eventually solve every puzzle.
Top-notch visuals and music score make for a very eerie atmosphere. Easily the best part about the game.
Absolutely zero replayability. Best when played through in a single sitting in my opinion. Try keeping a spoiler-free walkthrough handy if you don't like the idea of wandering aimlessly until you bump into a clue.
The plot is alright to excellent, depending on your personal taste, but I don't think anyone can call it poor.
If you like games such as The Stanley Parable, Dear Esther, or are otherwise interested in video games as an art, definitely pick this up if you catch it on sale. I can best summarize this game as being dropped into a gorgeous but gloomy lovecraftian film which you can explore and walk around in.
That all being said, it's definitely not for everyone. I personally see this game for all its worth but it's hard to 'recommend' it in the typical sense.

I am a fan of RTS, played COH1 and is still loving this, and have no complains at all.
The big hit of COH1 meant COH2 had a big shoe to fit and many expected abit too much.
Lets start with some basics, a decent campaing ( though some might disagree ) where there are straight-forward objectives and limited resources in a scenario settings. Quite linear but ive seen much worst and is definitely okay. Multiplayer is where the game shines. Co-op vs AI, Co-op vs players, 2v2 to 4v4. Its not anything innovative but is still done really well, fast-paced and definitely very enjoyable. If you ever have a bad day and just wanna troll then download a mod from the workshop and create a custom skirmish game. Its always fun spamming Railway arty at the enemy base at the start :)
Armies are mostly well balanced and thought about even though some fractions might seem op then the others but its just the different ways of using them. All fractions and their strength and weaknesses. Some are just more noob friendly and require less skills to win. But if you know your fraction well all fractions are enjoyable. It is just so fun adapting to the situation, map and your enemy troop type and react accordingly ^^ sometimes its frustrating when a granade kills your entire squad but hey, thats pretty realistic in a way. No infatry regarless of veterancy is granade-proof.
I never had server or connection problems even though im using a outdated wireless card and not even a cable. seldom dc which are my fault(which might be caused by teamates bad connection. Or mods. So check before you complain). Smooth gameplay. no glitches and such like Total War. immersive sounds and voice acting makes it really engaing :) you can hear a Tank in a frog of war. Troops would react to enemy actions(Enemy contact, granades, arty, etc.)  Or even hear the infanty groaning and whinning from long march or cold weathers.
Now the main thing everyone is upset about. The dlcs and expanion packs.
Thing is this game is not expensive if you compared to other games people wont blink and eye to buy. its $40 at base and like $75 for a GTA or Witcher3 ? Obviously they are different games but it just sees what you expect from the price. And i would say $40 base is a very worthy price for the time and effort programmers took to make this game. I am a programmer myself i know the pain.
DLCs, expensions, commanders and skins to expensive? Well you dont HAVE to buy them. A Tank with or without the skins is still exactly the same tank. There is no stats boost or buffs at all. It just makes yourself feel better. But honestly no one in the game really cares about your camo.
I understand some might be upset about the commanders. But it is really not such a big thing. "If you give a idiot a gun he will still lose a war. But if you give a veteran a small bayonet he can change an entire tide"- Milkshake3224
If you rely on your commanders to win a match then i feel really sad for you, because if you come in wanting to just wallet master your way through to be the best player you have come to the wrong game. I win many mutiplayer matches without even using my commanders as i dont see a need to. Unless fighting against some of the better players who know how to use their units. And NOT the derrogatory version, the real awesome.
This is a game where you have to think, strategize, and think more.
My main hint? Don't keep trying, or, at least, not the same things.
Too many reviews (the around 95% of the negatives) say that the game has too much RNG. The game decides whether you win, or you lose. While yes, this is partially true, look online. There are people who can beat the game reliably, NOT just on easy, but on medium.
Skill in this game comes from two things:
1. The ability to learn from your mistakes. This means that when you lose, you think about it and contemplate what you did wrong, and how you can improve.
2. The ability to work with difficult situations. Sometimes you are handed some bad luck. I'm trying to say that while that happens, being able to work with it is cruicial.
Both of these apply to the bad reviews. The problem with those, is that they were mostly complaining about RNG.
This game is awesome, so disregard that type of review.
One last note: don't get discouraged, keep on trying, perfecting, and especially, DON'T BLAME THE GAME FOR YOUR LOSS. One thing a lot of the bad reviews had in common was that they said that you could just die no matter how prepared you were. The fact of the matter is, that they weren't.
